title: Ingredient line parser
lead: Turn a free-text ingredient line into a `ParsedLine`: quantity with an optional upper bound, unit, item text, alternatives, notes, flags and a confidence score (ADR 0007, I1-I4).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** mapping to canonical items and writing rows (S17); the storage shape (S59); the review UI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Generating the shopping list needs structured ingredients. Being rule-based keeps it deterministic and testable. The result has the shape S59 stores: `qty` and `qty_max` for a range, the first choice as the item text, further choices as alternatives, and the flags and confidence columns of `ingredient_line`.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body: None if the items interview is done. Any lines that remain ambiguous get flagged for review, not guessed.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/larder/ingredients/parse.py`
- `src/larder/ingredients/units.py`
- `tests/test_ingredient_parse.py` (table-driven over every line in the fixtures)
- `tests/fixtures/ingredients/golden.toml` (the expected parse of every fixture line)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_quantities_integers_fractions_mixed_ranges` ("1 1/4", "2/3", "2-3" gives qty 2 and qty_max 3)
2. `test_unit_synonyms` (tbsp/tablespoon, tsp/teaspoons, lb/pound, cup/cups)
3. `test_package_with_size` ("1 can (15 oz) corn, no salt added")
4. `test_optional_flag` ("(optional)")
5. `test_alternatives` ("honey, maple syrup, or agave" gives item "honey" and alternatives ("maple syrup", "agave"))
6. `test_parenthetical_and_trailing_notes` ("(modify to taste)", ", chopped")
7. `test_non_food_flag` ("1 small mason jar")
8. `test_unparseable_line_low_confidence_not_exception`
9. `test_all_fixture_lines_parse_with_expected_results` (golden table)
10. `test_parsed_line_fields_match_the_ingredient_line_columns` (migrate a temporary database and check `qty`, `qty_max`, `notes`, `optional`, `is_food` and `confidence` exist; `alternatives` maps to `ingredient_line_alt`)
11. `test_confidence_penalties_are_applied_as_listed`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tokenize the quantity (unicode fractions and ranges too), unit (from the units table) and package-with-size pattern.
2. Remaining text becomes item text and notes (split on the first comma or parenthetical). A "x, y or z" item list becomes the first item plus alternatives.
3. Flags: optional, non-food (keyword list from ADR 0019).
4. Confidence is `1.0` minus penalties, floored at 0. Initial values, tuned against the golden table: unknown unit 0.3, missing quantity 0.2, unparsed leftover tokens 0.2, alternatives present 0.1. The review threshold comes from ADR 0019.
5. Return a frozen dataclass `ParsedLine(raw, qty, qty_max, unit, item_text, alternatives, notes, optional, is_food, confidence)`. Pure functions only; no DB. S17 resolves `unit` and items to ids and writes the rows, including `qty_max` and `ingredient_line_alt` (S59).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Parser tests pass; every line in the sample recipes is either parsed with high confidence or flagged.
- The golden table covers every range and alternatives form found in the fixtures.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
